articles.body: This chapter covers everything you need on day one: signing in, understanding the screen, and setting up your profile.

articles.title: Signing in
articles.body:
IAMS accepts your **work email** or your **domain username** together with your password. Where Active Directory is connected, your normal GBB network password works; otherwise the system checks the password stored in IAMS.

**Step 1.** Open IAMS in your browser. The **Welcome back** sign-in page appears.

![The IAMS sign-in page](/help/login-page.jpg)

**Step 2.** Type your work email or domain username in **Work email or Domain username**, then type your password in **Password**. Use the eye icon at the end of the password box to show or hide what you typed.

![Sign-in form filled in (the password is hidden)](/help/login-filled.jpg)

**Step 3.** Click **Sign in** (or press **Enter**). You land on your **Home** page.

![Home page after a successful sign-in (CAE view)](/help/dashboard-cae.jpg)

> **Tip:** Sign-in can take a few extra seconds, because IAMS first tries your directory (Active Directory) account and then falls back to the password stored in IAMS. Wait for the page to respond – do not click **Sign in** repeatedly.

> **Important:** If you see **Invalid credentials**, re-check your email/username and password. Repeated failures are recorded in the audit trail (see [section 15.4](/help/center?a=events)). If your account has been deactivated you will see **Account is deactivated** – contact your administrator.

### Two-factor verification

If two-factor authentication (2FA) is enabled for your account, a **Two-factor verification** screen appears after your password. Enter the 6-digit **Verification code** from your authenticator app, or choose to use a **Backup code** (format `xxxxx-xxxxx`) if you do not have your phone. On first use you are guided through an enrolment screen that shows a QR code to scan with your authenticator app.

### Forgot your password?

**Step 1.** On the sign-in page, click **Forgot password?**.

**Step 2.** Enter your work email in **Email address** and click **Send reset link**.

![Forgot-password page](/help/forgot-password.jpg)

**Step 3.** Open the email you receive and follow the link to the **Set a new password** page. Type the new password in **New password** and again in **Confirm password**, then save.

> **Important:** The reset link is time-limited. If it has expired, request a new one. Directory (Active Directory) users reset their password through the normal GBB network process, not through IAMS.

### Signing out

Click the **sign-out icon** next to your name at the bottom of the left-hand menu. If you ever suspect someone else has used your account, go to **Profile → Security → Log out everywhere** (see [section 1.6](/help/center?a=profile)).

articles.title: Finding your way around
articles.body:
IAMS has the same layout on every page.

![The IAMS screen: left menu, top bar and work area](/help/dashboard-top.jpg)

| Area | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Left menu** (green) | Your main navigation. Groups open and close when clicked. Only the items your role allows are shown. Red/green **number badges** show waiting items (e.g. approvals waiting for you). |
| **Top bar – page title** | Shows where you are. |
| **Top bar – Search…** | Opens the global search (shortcut **Ctrl + K**). |
| **Top bar – bell icon** | Your notifications; the number is how many are unread. |
| **Your name and role** | Top right, and at the bottom of the left menu. Click your name in the left menu to open your **Profile**. |
| **Collapse** | At the bottom of the left menu – shrinks the menu to icons to give you more room. |

### The left menu in detail

| Menu group | Contains | Chapter |
|---|---|---|
| **Home** | Your personal overview and to-dos | [section 1.3](/help/center?a=home) |
| **Workflow** | Review/Approval, Assignments, Escalations, Requests, Escalation Policies | [chapter 6](/help/center?a=ch-approvals), [chapter 16](/help/center?a=ch-workflow) |
| **Audit Lifecycle** | Audit Universe, Audit Programme, Engagements, Sampling, Findings, Reviews, Periodic Reports, Control Library, Evidence Repository | Part B |
| **Audit Modules** | Dedicated workspaces for System/IT, Financial and Compliance audits | [section 14.2](/help/center?a=domains) |
| **System Audit** | Toolkit overview, Data analytics, Access reviews, Event monitoring, Continuous monitoring, Security testing, System documentation | [section 15.1](/help/center?a=sysaudit) |
| **Notifications** | Alerts addressed to you | [section 1.5](/help/center?a=notif) |
| **Risk Register** | Enterprise risks | [section 17.1](/help/center?a=risk) |
| **How IAMS works** | A built-in one-page explanation of the lifecycle | [section 1.7](/help/center?a=help) |
| **System** | Assets, Documents, Analytics, Audit Logs, Users, Integrations, Audit intelligence, Settings | Parts D and E |

> **Tip:** Hover your mouse over any menu item for a one-line description of what it is for.

articles.title: Your Home page
articles.body:
**Home** is your landing page. It starts with “what needs *you*” and then shows the wider audit programme. The sections you see depend on your role.

![Home page – Quick Actions, My Work, Findings by Severity, Audit intelligence](/help/dashboard-top.jpg)

| Section | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Start audit** button (top right) | Opens the Start-audit wizard ([section 7.2](/help/center?a=wizard)). Only for people allowed to create engagements. |
| **Quick Actions** | One-click shortcuts: Start audit, Audit plans, Findings, Register risk, Review approvals, Raise request, Documents, Add asset. You only see the actions your role may perform. |
| **My Work** | Active engagements you lead or are assigned to, your supporting assignments, and approvals waiting for you. |
| **Findings by Severity** | Open findings split into Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational. |
| **Audit intelligence** | Early-warning signals, e.g. “Engagement may miss its OLA”. Click **Open** for the full list ([section 21.1](/help/center?a=predictive)). |

Scroll down for programme-level indicators (for oversight roles):

![Home page lower half – KPI cards, Programme Health, Risk Heat Map, Top Risks](/help/dashboard-bottom.jpg)

- **Total Engagements, Open Findings, Total Risks, Pending Approvals** – headline numbers.
- **Programme Health** – high-risk coverage, follow-up verified %, average cycle time, average review-issue time, working papers awaiting review, overdue follow-ups.
- **Risk Heat Map** – open and mitigated risks plotted by likelihood × impact.
- **Top Risks** – the highest-scoring risks with owner and status. Click **View all** for the Risk Register.

Auditees see a simplified Home page – see [section 11.1](/help/center?a=auditee).

articles.title: Global search and the command palette
articles.body:
You can jump to any page, engagement, finding, risk, asset or person without using the menu.

**Step 1.** Click **Search…** in the top bar, or press **Ctrl + K** (⌘ + K may also work on a Mac keyboard).

**Step 2.** Type part of a name or reference number. Results appear grouped; with nothing typed, the box lists the pages you can go to.

![Search palette showing the “Go to” list](/help/cmd-palette.jpg)

**Step 3.** Use the **↑ ↓** keys and **Enter**, or click a result. Press **Esc** to close.

articles.title: Notifications
articles.body:
IAMS sends you in-app notifications for approvals, stage changes, assignments, escalations and comments. Click the **bell** or choose **Notifications** in the menu.

![Notifications page](/help/notifications.jpg)

- Use the **All** and **Unread** tabs to filter.
- Click **Mark all read** to clear the unread count.

![After Mark all read: “Marked 47 notifications as read”](/help/notifications-marked.jpg)
- Each notification shows a short title, the detail, and its age (e.g. “3 days ago”).

> **Tip:** The bell badge and the left-menu badges refresh automatically every 15 seconds – you do not need to reload the page.

articles.title: Your profile
articles.body:
Click your name at the bottom of the left menu to open **Profile**. It has four tabs.

### Profile tab

![Profile tab](/help/profile-top.jpg)

Edit your **Display name**, **Phone** and **Skills** (type a skill and press Enter or comma – skills help the system suggest you for suitable audits), then click **Save profile**. Name, email, department and job title are shown greyed because they come from your directory record.

### Signature tab

Your signature is stamped on documents you approve. You can **Draw** it with the mouse (or finger on touch screens) or **Upload** a PNG/JPG (a transparent PNG looks best).

![Signature tab with the drawing box](/help/profile-signature.jpg)

1. Draw your signature in the box. Use **Clear** to start again.
2. Click **Use signature**. A “Signature saved” message confirms it.

> **Tip:** You can also create your signature the first time you approve something – the approval panel offers the same drawing box ([section 6.2](/help/center?a=approve-do)).

### Security tab

![Security tab – change password and sessions](/help/profile-security.jpg)

- **Change Password** (for accounts with an IAMS-stored password): enter **Current password**, **New password**, **Confirm password**, then **Change password**.
- **Sessions → Log out everywhere** ends every active browser session for your account. Use it on a shared computer or if you lose a device.

### Access tab

![Access tab – roles and effective permissions](/help/profile-access.jpg)

Shows your **Assigned Roles** and every **Effective Permission** (for example `engagement:read`). Use it to understand why a button is or is not available to you.

articles.title: Getting help inside IAMS
articles.body:
IAMS has help built in. You never need to leave the system to find out how to do something.

### The Help Centre

Choose **Help Centre** in the left menu (or press **g** then **c**). Type a question the way you would ask a colleague – for example “why can't I approve my own submission” – and press **Enter**.

![The Help Centre – ask a question, pick a task for your role, or browse the guide](/help/help-centre-landing.jpg)

- **Try asking** – example questions you can click.
- **For your role** and **Everyone** – the most common tasks, tailored to what your role can do.
- **Browse the guide** – every chapter of this manual, with its topics listed on the left once you open one.

Results are ranked, with a **Best match** at the top and a short excerpt showing where your words were found:

![Search results for a question](/help/help-centre-results.jpg)

Open a result to read the full step-by-step guide with screenshots. Click any screenshot to enlarge it. Use the **previous / next** buttons at the bottom to carry on reading.

![A guide page – numbered steps, screenshots and the guide contents on the left](/help/help-article-checklists.jpg)

> **Tip:** The Help Centre uses the same content as this manual and works offline from the application – it does not send your questions anywhere.

### The “?” button on every page

The round **?** icon in the top bar opens the guide for **the screen you are on**. On an engagement's *Checklists* tab it opens “Checklists – testing controls”; on *Working Papers* it opens the working-paper guide; in *Settings* it opens the guide for the tab you are viewing.

### Ask from the search box

Press **Ctrl K** (or **/**) and type a question of three or more words. Matching **Help** topics appear at the top of the results, followed by matching records:

![Typing a question into search shows matching help topics](/help/help-palette-question.jpg)

### Keyboard shortcuts

Press **?** (Shift + /) anywhere outside a text box to see the shortcut sheet:

![The keyboard shortcut sheet](/help/help-shortcuts-sheet.jpg)

| Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Ctrl K** or **/** | Open search (records, pages, and help) |
| **?** | Show or hide the shortcut sheet |
| **Esc** | Close a panel, dialog or the search box |
| **g** then **h** | Go to Home |
| **g** then **a** | Approvals |
| **g** then **e** | Engagements |
| **g** then **f** | Findings |
| **g** then **p** | Audit Programme |
| **g** then **u** | Audit Universe |
| **g** then **v** | Reviews |
| **g** then **r** | Risk Register |
| **g** then **q** | Requests |
| **g** then **s** | Assets |
| **g** then **l** | Audit Logs |
| **g** then **n** | Notifications |
| **g** then **m** | My profile |
| **g** then **c** | Help Centre |

The sheet only lists the destinations your role can open. Shortcuts are switched off while you are typing in a field.

### The “Getting started” checklist

On **Home**, staff see a short checklist for their first week, matched to their role – for example, an auditor is guided to add a signature, open an engagement, test a control, write a working paper and raise a finding. Each item links to the page **and** to a **How** guide.

![The Getting started checklist on Home](/help/dashboard-getting-started.jpg)

Tick items as you finish them. Click **×** to hide the checklist; to bring it back, open the Help Centre and choose **Show the getting-started checklist on Home again**. Your ticks are stored in your own browser only.

### How IAMS works

Choose **How IAMS works** in the menu for a one-page explanation of the six lifecycle stages and who does what at each.

![How IAMS works page](/help/help.jpg)

articles.title: Roles and permissions
articles.body: IAMS decides what you see from your **role**. Your administrator assigns one or more roles to each user. Menu items, buttons and even tabs appear or disappear according to the permissions in your roles.
articles.text: IAMS decides what you see from your role . Your administrator assigns one or more roles to each user. Menu items, buttons and even tabs appear or disappear according to the permissions in your roles.

articles.title: The roles
articles.body:
| Role | Who it is for | In one sentence |
|---|---|---|
| **super_admin** | System administrators / Chief Audit Executive office | Full access to everything, including users, roles and settings. |
| **audit_manager** | Audit managers | Plans the programme, creates and oversees engagements, approves working papers, verifies follow-up, issues reviews. |
| **audit_lead** | Lead auditors | Runs fieldwork on assigned engagements, approves working papers at team level, closes findings, creates the review. |
| **auditor** | Staff auditors | Does the testing: checklists, working papers, evidence, and raises findings. |
| **cae** | Chief Audit Executive | Approves programmes, gives oversight approval and **issues** audit reviews; sees all engagements. |
| **director** | Directors / executive oversight | Read-wide oversight and **final** approval of reviews; authorises security tests. |
| **auditee** | The people and departments being audited | Responds to findings, uploads remediation evidence, supplies requested documents, attests to assets. |
| **viewer** | Default read-only access | Can see dashboards, programme, engagements, findings and reviews, but change nothing. |
| **audit_committee** | Audit Committee members | Periodic oversight pack and dashboard only. |

> **Tip:** Open **Profile → Access** ([section 1.6](/help/center?a=profile)) to see exactly which roles and permissions *you* hold.

articles.chapter: The audit lifecycle at a glance
articles.title: The audit lifecycle at a glance
articles.body:
Before using individual screens, understand the path every audit follows. IAMS moves an engagement forward **automatically** once the requirements of the current stage are met – the only manual steps are **Start fieldwork** and **Issue the review**.

| # | Stage | Where in IAMS | Who does the work |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Audit Universe** – the list of things that can be audited, each with a risk score | Audit Lifecycle → Audit Universe | Audit managers maintain; everyone reads |
| 2 | **Audit Programme** – the annual plan of audits, approved before work starts | Audit Lifecycle → Audit Programme | Manager drafts → CAE approves |
| 3 | **Engagement (fieldwork)** – one engagement = one audit: checklists, working papers, evidence | Audit Lifecycle → Engagements | Lead auditor and team; manager reviews |
| 4 | **Findings** – issues raised, each assigned to an auditee | Engagement → Findings, and Audit Lifecycle → Findings | Auditors raise; auditee responds |
| 5 | **Review** – the audit report, signed through the approval chain, then issued | Engagement → Review | Lead drafts → manager/CAE/director approve → CAE or manager issues |
| 6 | **Follow-up & closure** – auditee fixes issues, auditor verifies, findings close, engagement closes | Engagement → Follow-up | Auditee remediates; auditor verifies; manager closes |

articles.title: Engagement status and the five-stage tracker
articles.body:
Every engagement shows a tracker at the top of its page with five stages:

![The stage tracker, the “What's next” panel and the engagement tabs](/help/eng-overview.jpg)

| Tracker stage | Status badge you will see | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Planning & Setup** | **Planned** | Created and scheduled; fieldwork not started. |
| **Fieldwork & Testing** | **In Progress** | Checklists are being tested, working papers written, evidence captured. |
| **Quality Assurance** | **Under review / Quality assurance** | All testing is done and working papers approved; the work is being quality-checked. |
| **Review & Findings** | **Review Issued** | The audit review has been issued to stakeholders; findings are being remediated. |
| **Audit Closure** | **Closed** | Every finding is closed and the engagement is closed. |

### The “What's next” panel

Directly under the tracker, **What's next** names the *exact* thing the engagement is waiting for, and who it is waiting on – for example:

- “The audit team to finish testing controls (1/43 done).”
- “The audit team to revise and resubmit 1 rejected working paper.”
- “Adaeze Okonkwo to approve working papers (0/1 approved).”

> **Tip:** If an engagement looks stuck, open it and read **What's next**. It always tells you the blocking requirement.

### The gates (rules for moving forward)

By default, IAMS enforces these gates (an administrator can relax them in Settings → Audit Customization, see [section 24.5](/help/center?a=cust)):

1. **In Progress → Quality Assurance** – *all* checklist controls have a result (nothing left “Not tested”) **and** *all* working papers are approved.
2. **Quality Assurance → Review Issued** – the audit review must be **issued** (a deliberate human act).
3. **Review Issued → Closed** – *every* finding on the engagement is **Closed**.

articles.title: The Start-audit wizard
articles.body:
*Who can do this: super admin, audit manager.* Click **Start audit** on the Engagements page or on Home. A four-step panel opens.

### Step 1 of 4 – Scope

You can start an audit **from a plan item** (normal route) or **ad-hoc** (outside the approved programme).

![Scope step – From plan item: pick the approved Plan, then the Plan item](/help/wizard-1-plan-item.jpg)

**From plan item:** choose the **Plan** (an approved programme) and then the **Plan item** (the entity to be audited). The entity, type and priority come from the plan.

**Ad-hoc:** click **Ad-hoc**. Choose the **Auditable entity**, the **Audit type**, the **Priority**, and give an **Ad-hoc reason** – this is required, because the audit is outside the annual plan (for example an incident or a management request).

![Ad-hoc scope – entity, type, priority and the required reason](/help/wizard-1-adhoc-filled.jpg)

Click **Next**.

### Step 2 of 4 – Team & schedule

![Team & schedule step](/help/wizard-2-empty.jpg)

1. **Title** – a clear name for the engagement.
2. **Lead auditor** – owns fieldwork. The list is **ranked by skill match, workload and capacity**, and shows how many active engagements each person already has.

![Lead auditor choices with workload shown](/help/wizard-2-lead-options.jpg)

3. **Audit manager** – reviews and signs off the lead's work. The list shows only people who can approve.
4. **Auditee** – the primary contact in the audited area who provides evidence and management responses.
5. **Supporting auditors** (optional) – search by name or skill and click **Add**; the button turns to **✔ Added**.
6. **Planned start**, **Planned end** and **OLA deadline** (all required; the OLA defaults to the end date).
7. **Budgeted hours** (optional) – the team logs actual hours against this budget.

![Step 2 completed](/help/wizard-2-filled.jpg)

Click **Next**.

### Step 3 of 4 – Review

![Review step – summary and pre-loaded checklist controls](/help/wizard-3-review.jpg)

A summary of the choices is shown, followed by the **Checklist controls**. IAMS **pre-fills** the checklist from the template for the audit type (for example 25 controls for a Compliance audit). You can:

- edit any control's reference, statement or test procedure, or remove it with the bin icon;
- **Add control** to type your own;
- **Upload Act / Policy** to have controls extracted from a document;
- **Import from Control Library** – pick a framework (ISO 27001, NIST, COBIT…) and **Import Framework**.

Click **Create engagement**.

### Step 4 of 4 – Launch

![Launch step – engagement created](/help/wizard-4-launch.jpg)

The engagement receives the next reference number (e.g. **AUD-2027-002**) and the team is notified. Choose:

- **Save & review later** – leaves it in **Planned** status; or
- **Start fieldwork** – moves it straight to **In Progress**.

articles.title: Checklists – testing controls
articles.body:
The **Checklists** tab is the control-test register. Each row is one control with its reference (e.g. `GDPR-ART28`), the control statement, the test procedure, a result drop-down, a notes box, and evidence buttons.

![Checklist tab on a new engagement – 0 of 25 tested](/help/demo-checklists.jpg)

The bar at the top shows **% tested** and counts of **passed**, **failed**, **tested** and **not tested**.

### Record a test result

**Step 1.** Find the control. Read the **test procedure** (the grey text under the statement).

**Step 2.** Open the result drop-down (it starts at **Not tested**) and choose **Passed**, **Failed** or **Not applicable**.

**Step 3.** Optionally type **Notes…**.

**Step 4.** For a **Failed** control, two buttons appear: **Attach evidence** (highlighted until you attach something) and **Raise finding**.

![A control marked Failed shows “Attach evidence” and “Raise finding”](/help/demo-checklist-failed.jpg)

> **Tip:** Use **Bulk update the untested controls** (above the list) to mark every remaining “Not tested” control as **Passed** or **Not applicable** in one action – useful for controls that genuinely do not apply to this entity. The system confirms how many were updated.

### Add and import controls

- **Add Control** – type a reference, statement and test procedure.
- **Upload Act / Policy** – upload a statute or policy document; IAMS extracts candidate controls for you to review and import.
- **Import from Control Library** – choose a framework and import all its controls ([section 13.1](/help/center?a=library)).

### Raise a finding from a failed control

**Step 1.** On the failed control, click **Raise finding**. The **New finding** panel opens, **pre-filled** with a title and description taken from the control, the **Category**, a default **Severity** and the **Source control test**.

![New finding panel – title and description already filled in from the control](/help/finding-form-top.jpg)

**Step 2.** Complete the required fields:

| Field | What to write |
|---|---|
| **Title** | A short, specific statement of the issue. |
| **Description** | What you found and how you tested it. |
| **Category** / **Severity** | Choose the audit category and Critical, High, Medium, Low or Informational. |
| **Source control test / Source working paper** | Links the finding back to its evidence chain. |
| **Related risk** | Optional – link the Risk Register item this finding relates to. |
| **Root cause** | *Why* it happened. |
| **Risk implication** | What could go wrong because of it. |
| **Recommendation** | What the auditee should do. |
| **Auditee** | Who must respond. (Add more under **Additional auditees** to name co-responders.) |
| **Due date** | When remediation is due. |

![Finding form completed, ready to raise](/help/finding-form-filled.jpg)

**Step 3.** Click **Raise finding**. A “Finding created” message appears and the control row now shows **Finding raised**.

![The control now shows “Finding raised”](/help/finding-created.jpg)

articles.title: Working papers
articles.body:
A **working paper** documents what you did and concluded for a test. Papers are written in a built-in Word-style editor and must be **approved by a manager** before the engagement can move to quality assurance.

![Working Papers tab – an existing paper that was rejected, with the reason shown](/help/eng-working-papers.jpg)

Buttons on this tab: **Sampling tool** ([section 8.1](/help/center?a=sampling)), **Import** (bring in a document) and **New working paper**.

### Write a working paper

**Step 1.** Click **New working paper**. The editor opens full-screen with a header showing the engagement reference, author and version (**v1.0 – DRAFT**).

![The working-paper editor, loaded with the audit type's template](/help/wp-editor-new.jpg)

**Step 2.** Type a title in **Working Paper Title** (top-left). Use **Template** (top bar) to switch template, and **Insert Controls (25)** to bring the engagement's control list into the paper.

**Step 3.** Fill in each numbered section. The toolbar offers the usual Word-style tools: paragraph style, font, size, bold/italic/underline, colour, alignment, bullets, indent, **Table**, **Insert Image** and **Page Break**. **Header & Footer** and **Fullscreen Studio** open extra layout options.

**Step 4.** Click **Save as Draft**. A “Saved as draft” message appears and you return to the list.

![Draft saved – buttons: Open in Editor, Export PDF, Submit](/help/wp-saved-draft.jpg)

### Submit for review

Click **Submit** on the paper (or **Submit for Review** inside the editor). The status becomes **Submitted**; the audit manager is notified and the paper appears in their approval inbox.

![Submitted – the paper is now read-only (View / Export PDF)](/help/wp-submitted.jpg)

> **Important:** While a paper is **Submitted** you cannot edit it. If it is **Rejected**, the manager's reason is shown on the row; revise and resubmit.

### Reviewing a working paper (manager)

The manager opens **Workflow → Review/Approval**, finds the **Audit Working Paper** row, and uses **Approve & Sign** or **Reject** as described in [section 6.2](/help/center?a=approve-do).

![The manager's inbox with the submitted working paper](/help/manager-approvals-inbox.jpg)

![Approve panel with the manager's saved signature](/help/manager-approve-panel.jpg)

After approval the **What's next** list no longer asks for working-paper approval – the only remaining requirement here is to finish the checklist.

![Engagement after the working paper was approved](/help/eng-after-wp-approved.jpg)

articles.title: Evidence requests (asking the auditee for documents)
articles.body:
Instead of chasing documents by email, ask for them in IAMS and track them.

**Step 1.** Open the **Evidence Requests** tab and click **New request**.

![New evidence request form](/help/evreq-form-empty.jpg)

**Step 2.** Complete the form:

- **What do you need?** (required) – e.g. “Signed processor contracts for top 10 vendors”.
- **Details (optional)** – period, format, or anything that helps find the right document.
- **Due date (optional)**.
- **Request from** – defaults to the engagement's auditee.

![Request form completed](/help/evreq-form-filled.jpg)

**Step 3.** Click **Send request**. The request appears with status **Open**; you can **Upload** a file against it yourself or **Cancel** it.

![Request sent – status Open](/help/evreq-sent.jpg)

**What happens next.** The auditee sees the request at the top of their Home page under **Documents requested from you**, opens the engagement's **Evidence Requests** tab, and uploads the file against the request (“Document submitted — the auditor will review it”). You then **accept** it (“Request fulfilled”) or **return** it to the auditee if it is not what you asked for. Accepted files are stored with the engagement's evidence. The auditee's side is described in [section 11.1](/help/center?a=auditee).

articles.title: Audit sampling
articles.body:
Checking every payment, invoice or access log is usually impractical. **Sampling** lets you test a smaller, defensible selection and *prove* how it was chosen. IAMS stores the population file and the sample as engagement evidence, and records the method and **seed** so anyone can reproduce the same sample.

There are two entry points: the stand-alone **Audit Lifecycle → Sampling** page, and the **Sampling tool** button on an engagement's **Working Papers** tab. They use the same engine.

articles.title: Step 1 – How many items should you test?
articles.body:
Open **Audit Lifecycle → Sampling**.

![The Sampling page: Step 1 sample-size calculator and Step 2 draw](/help/sampling-page.jpg)

The page opens with a short explanation (“What is audit sampling?”) and then the calculator, which is pure planning – no file needed.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Population size** | Total items in scope (e.g. 1000 payments). |
| **Confidence** | How sure you want to be (e.g. 95%). |
| **Tolerable rate** | The maximum error rate you would accept (0.05 = 5%). |
| **Expected rate** | Errors you actually expect (optional; 0 if blank). |

articles.title: How a finding moves
articles.body:
1. **Auditor raises** the finding. It stays internal until the review is issued ([section 3.2](/help/center?a=findingflow)).
2. **Review is issued**; the auditee can now see the finding and is notified.
3. **Auditee responds** with a management response and uploads remediation evidence ([section 11.1](/help/center?a=auditee)).
4. **Auditor/lead verifies** the evidence ([section 9.4](/help/center?a=finding-close)).
5. **Closure** is sent for approval and the finding becomes **Closed**.
6. When all findings are closed, the engagement can be **closed** (chapter [section 3.1](/help/center?a=stages)).

articles.title: Verify remediation and close a finding
articles.body:
*Who can do this: audit manager, audit lead, super admin.*

**Step 1.** Open the finding (or the engagement's **Follow-up** tab). When its status is **Management Response Received** or **In Remediation**, a **Verify** button is available. (While it is still **Open** you will see “Waiting for the auditee's response”.)

**Step 2.** Review the auditee's **Management response** and the remediation evidence.

**Step 3.** Click **Verify**. A small form appears with the radio buttons **Verified** (default) and **Rejected**, and a **Notes** box. Write what you checked and click **Save verification** (“Verification recorded”). If you choose **Rejected** the auditee is told what is still missing and can upload more evidence.

![Verified](/help/followup-verification-recorded.jpg)

**Step 4.** Once the evidence is verified, click **Request closure** at the top right of the finding page. A “Finding closure sent for approval” message appears; the request goes to the approval inbox ([section 6.2](/help/center?a=approve-do)), and the finding becomes **Closed** when it is approved.

![A verified finding with the Request closure button](/help/finding-verified-request-closure.jpg)

![Closure sent – status Pending Closure](/help/finding-closure-sent.jpg)

By default the closure is approved by the **engagement manager** (Settings → Audit Customization → Approval Matrix → *Finding Closure*).

> **Important:** An engagement cannot be **Closed** until *every* finding on it is **Closed**.

articles.title: Create, approve and issue a review
articles.body:
*Draft and submit: audit manager or audit lead. Approve: lead/manager (level 1) and CAE (level 2). Issue: CAE or audit manager.* The review can be drafted once the engagement has reached **Quality Assurance** – the “What's next” panel will say so. A full worked run is in chapter [chapter 12](/help/center?a=ch-example).

**Step 1 – Open the Review tab.** While no review exists, the tab shows the **Audit Report – Word Document Editor**. IAMS has already filled it from the default template with the engagement details and every finding.

![The Review tab before a report exists – template, title, sign-off choice and pre-filled editor](/help/review-tab-signoff-options.jpg)

**Step 2 – Choose template, title and sign-off route.**

- **Report template** – defaults to *GBB Standard Audit Report*; others are listed in the drop-down ([section 24.3](/help/center?a=set-review)).
- **Report title** – required.
- **Report Sign-Off Requirement:**

| Mode | Approval chain |
|---|---|
| **Oversight Sign-Off Only (1 Executive Level)** – *Standard audit* | Reviewed by the engagement audit manager, then signed off by the oversight approver (`report:approve:oversight`, e.g. Head of Internal Audit / CAE). |
| **Oversight + Executive Final Sign-Off (2 Executive Levels)** – *Executive / major audit* | Manager review, oversight endorsement, **and** final sign-off by `report:approve:final` (e.g. Director General / MD). |

**Step 3 – Check the draft.** Use **Re-sync Findings & Auditee Responses into Document** to refresh the findings table (the card tells you how many findings and auditee responses are linked). Scroll the editor to read it: executive summary table, background, objectives and scope, methodology, summary of findings, detailed findings (category, status, due date, auditee, observation, root cause, risk, recommendation and the auditee's management response), and conclusion.

![The generated report body](/help/review-generated-body.jpg)

**Step 4 – Generate.** Click **Generate Audit Report** (bottom right of the editor) – or **Save as Draft** to keep working. The report is saved as **Draft v1** and the Review tab now offers: **Word Editor / Preview / Cards**, **Open Word Studio**, **View PDF**, **Export PDF**, **Save Draft** and **Submit for approval**. “What's next” changes to “…to submit the review for sign-off.”

![A draft review – action buttons across the top](/help/review-draft-toolbar.jpg)

**Step 5 – Submit.** Click **Submit for approval** (“Submitted for approval”). The report locks and appears in the approvers' inboxes.

**Step 6 – Approve.** Each level is actioned in the inbox ([section 6.2](/help/center?a=approve-do)). The first level (`report:approve`) can be given by the lead auditor, audit manager or super admin **other than the person who submitted**; the second level (`report:approve:oversight`) by the CAE. An approver who rejects must give a **Rejection reason** and the author revises and resubmits.

**Step 7 – Issue.** When every level has signed, the Review tab shows **Approved**, the **Signed document** and an **Issue review** button. Click it (“Audit report formally issued”). The engagement becomes **Review Issued**; the auditee is notified and can now see their findings.

![Approved and ready to issue](/help/review-approved-issue-button.jpg)

![Issued](/help/review-issued.jpg)

> **Important:** Issuing is a deliberate human act. The engagement cannot reach **Review Issued** without it.

### The Word Studio editor

Both the Review tab and the working-paper screen use the same Word-style editor. **Open Word Studio** (or **Fullscreen Studio**) opens it full screen.

![Word Studio – top bar, sign-off choice, toolbar and the page](/help/review-studio.jpg)

| Area | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Exit Editor** (top-left) | Leaves the studio. If there are unsaved changes you are asked first. |
| **Title and status badge** | The document title, with **Draft** or **Submitted**. |
| **Template** | Switch template; **Re-sync (n)** refreshes findings and responses into the document. |
| **Export DOCX** | Downloads the document as a Word file. |
| **Save Draft / Submit for Approval** | Save without submitting, or send to the approval chain. |
| **Toolbar row** | Paragraph style, font, size, bold, italic, underline, strike-through, text colour, highlight, clear formatting, alignment, bulleted and numbered lists, indent/outdent, **Margins**, zoom (e.g. 1.5×). |
| **Table** | Inserts a 2×2, 3×3, 4×4 or 5×5 table, or a custom rows × columns grid; with the cursor inside a table you can add a row below, add a column, delete the row or delete the table. |
| **Insert Image** | Adds an inline picture. |
| **Page Break** (Ctrl+Enter) | Starts a new page. |
| **Header & Footer** | Shows the template's header (organisation, classification) and footer. |
| **Status bar** (bottom) | Page x of y, word and character count, margins, “Print Layout · Ready”. |

![The Table tool](/help/review-studio-table.jpg)

![A submitted report – the editor is read-only while it awaits approval](/help/review-studio-submitted.jpg)

articles.title: What you need to do
articles.body:
Your **Home** page opens with a short guide, **What you need to do here**:

1. Review any **findings** assigned to you and submit your **management response** with a remediation plan.
2. When you have fixed an issue, open the finding and **upload your remediation evidence** – the auditor will verify it.

- **Quick Actions** – **Raise request** and **Documents**.
- **My Work** – the engagements you are the auditee of, with their status and OLA date.
- **Findings by Severity** – your open findings.

articles.title: Respond to a finding
articles.body:
A finding becomes visible to you **after the audit review has been issued**; you are notified when that happens.

**Step 1.** Choose **Audit Lifecycle → Findings**. You see only findings raised against you.

![Findings assigned to the auditee](/help/auditee-findings.jpg)

**Step 2.** Click a finding. Read the **description, root cause, risk implication** and **recommendation**, and note the **due date**.

**Step 3.** In the **Follow-up** panel on the right, type your **Management response** – describe the planned remediation, the owner and the timeline – and click **Submit response**. (A response cannot be empty.)

![The auditee's Follow-up panel – management response and remediation evidence](/help/auditee-finding-response.jpg)

**Step 4.** When the fix is done, under **Remediation evidence** click **Choose File**, select a document or screenshot proving the remediation, and click **Upload evidence**.

**Step 5.** The auditor reviews and **verifies** your evidence. If it is not enough, they reject it with notes and you can upload more. Once verified, the finding is closed through approval.

> **Important:** Respond **before the due date**. Overdue findings are flagged, appear on management dashboards and can escalate to senior management ([section 16.3](/help/center?a=escalations)).

articles.title: Worked example: one audit from start to finish
articles.body:
This chapter follows **one real audit through every stage**, step by step, exactly as it was performed in IAMS during the preparation of this manual. Use it as a practice script for training. Each step names **who** does it, because IAMS deliberately makes different people act at different points (segregation of duties – see [section 6.5](/help/center?a=sod)).

**The scenario.** Management asks Internal Audit to look at cash-reconciliation controls in the Treasury department. The audit is *ad-hoc* (not in the annual plan), is a **Compliance Audit**, and ends with one finding about data-processing contracts.

| Role in the example | Account type | What they do |
|---|---|---|
| Audit manager | `audit_manager` | Starts the audit, approves the working paper, drafts the review, approves the finding closure |
| Lead auditor | `audit_lead` | Runs fieldwork, gives first-level approval of the review, verifies remediation, requests closure |
| CAE | `cae` | Gives oversight sign-off and **issues** the review |
| Auditee | `auditee` | Responds to the finding, uploads remediation evidence and requested documents |

> **Important:** Because nobody can approve their own submission, a single person **cannot** run this whole example alone. You need at least four sign-ins (manager, lead, CAE, auditee).

articles.title: Step 3 – Do the fieldwork (lead, manager and team)
articles.body:
**3.1 Test a control and raise a finding.** On the **Checklists** tab mark the control that does not pass as **Failed**; click **Raise finding**, complete root cause, risk implication, recommendation, auditee and due date, and click **Raise finding** ([section 7.4](/help/center?a=checklists)).

![A failed control with its “Attach evidence” and “Raise finding” buttons](/help/demo-checklist-failed.jpg)

**3.2 Write a working paper.** On **Working Papers → New working paper** write the paper in the editor, **Save as Draft**, then **Submit** ([section 7.5](/help/center?a=wp)).

![The working-paper editor](/help/wp-editor-new.jpg)

**3.3 Ask the auditee for documents.** On **Evidence Requests → New request** describe what you need and send it ([section 7.7](/help/center?a=evreq)).

![Evidence request sent](/help/evreq-sent.jpg)

**3.4 Approve the working paper (manager).** The manager finds the paper in **Workflow → Review/Approval** and approves it.

![The manager's inbox with the submitted working paper](/help/manager-approvals-inbox.jpg)

**3.5 Finish testing.** When every other control has a result, use the bulk action **Bulk update the untested controls**, choose **Passed** and click **Apply to all untested**. IAMS asks you to confirm because this records a result for controls that were not tested one by one.

![Confirmation before marking the remaining controls as Passed](/help/checklist-bulk-confirm.jpg)

As soon as all checklist controls have a result **and** all working papers are approved, the engagement moves **by itself** to **Quality Assurance**, and **What's next** now says the lead should draft the review:

![The engagement has advanced to Quality Assurance](/help/engagement-qa-stage.jpg)

articles.title: Step 4 – Draft, approve and issue the review
articles.body:
**4.1 Draft the review.** Open the **Review** tab. IAMS has already pre-loaded the report template with the engagement details and the findings. Choose the **Report Sign-Off Requirement** (here *Oversight Sign-Off Only*), check the text, and click **Generate Audit Report**.

![Review tab – template, title, sign-off choice and the pre-loaded editor](/help/review-tab-signoff-options.jpg)

![The generated report text, including each finding with root cause, risk and recommendation](/help/review-generated-body.jpg)

**4.2 Edit in Word Studio.** Click **Open Word Studio** for a full-screen editor with the same tools as Word: styles, fonts, tables (**Table** inserts 2×2 to 5×5 grids or a custom size, with +Row, +Column, Delete Row/Table tools), **Insert Image**, **Page Break**, margins and zoom ([section 10.3](/help/center?a=review-flow)).

![Word Studio full-screen editor](/help/review-studio.jpg)

![The Table tool](/help/review-studio-table.jpg)

**4.3 Submit for approval.** Click **Submit for Approval** (in Word Studio) or **Submit for approval** on the Review tab. The status changes to **Submitted**.

![Submitted – the report is locked while approvers review it](/help/review-studio-submitted.jpg)

**4.4 First-level approval (lead auditor).** Because the manager submitted the review, the manager cannot also approve it. The first level (`report:approve`) is actioned by the **lead auditor**. A CAE looking at the inbox at this moment sees nothing – the item has not reached the CAE's level yet:

![The CAE's inbox is empty until level 1 is signed](/help/approvals-cae-empty-wronglevel.jpg)

The lead opens the item (shown as **Level 1 of 2**), adds a comment and clicks **Approve & Sign**:

![The lead auditor's approval panel with the saved signature](/help/approvals-lead-panel.jpg)

![Level 1 approved](/help/approvals-lead-done.jpg)

**4.5 Oversight approval (CAE).** The item now appears for the CAE as **Level 2 of 2**.

![Level 2 of 2 waiting for the CAE](/help/approvals-cae-level2.jpg)

**4.6 Issue the review (CAE).** After the CAE approves, the Review tab shows the status **Approved**, the frozen **Signed document**, and an **Issue review** button, and **What's next** reads “Review approved and ready to issue to the auditee.”

![Approved and ready to issue](/help/review-approved-issue-button.jpg)

Click **Issue review**. A message confirms “Audit report formally issued”, the engagement becomes **Review Issued** and the auditee is notified.

![The review is issued](/help/review-issued.jpg)

articles.title: Control Library
articles.body:
The **Control Library** is the central catalogue of controls and the frameworks they belong to. It feeds the checklists in every engagement and shows how much of each framework has actually been tested.

Choose **Audit Lifecycle → Control Library**.

![Control Library – frameworks, controls and coverage](/help/control-library.jpg)

**Headline numbers:** **Frameworks** (here 15), **Total controls** (71) and **Active controls** (71).

**Coverage by framework** – one tile per framework (COBIT, GBB-FIN, GBB-SYS, GDPR, ISO/IEC 20000, ISO 22301, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 31000, ISO 9001, NDPR, NIST CSF, NITDA, PCI DSS, SOX ITGC …), showing *how many of its controls are in the library* (e.g. 22/22) and its domain (IT Audit, Compliance, Governance, Financial).

**Assurance coverage (tested)** – below the tiles, one bar per framework shows the share of controls that have been **tested** in engagements, with the **pass** and **fail** counts, and an overall figure (here “75% overall · 53/71 controls”). Use it to see which frameworks have been audited and where failures cluster.

### Add controls

- **New control** – add a single control (framework, reference, statement, test procedure).
- **Upload Act / Policy / Framework** – upload a document; IAMS extracts candidate controls, which you review before importing.

> **Tip:** Importing a framework into an engagement's checklist is done from the engagement ([section 7.4](/help/center?a=checklists)) – the library itself is the source.

articles.title: Choosing the right audit type
articles.body: When you create a programme or an engagement you choose an **audit type**. The type decides which **checklist controls** are pre-loaded, which **working-paper template** is suggested, which findings categories apply, and which **escalation timings** are used. Choose carefully, because everything downstream follows from it.

The type decides which checklist controls are pre-loaded, which working-paper template is suggested, which findings categories apply, and which escalation timings are used. articles.title: Audit types guide
articles.body:
| Audit type | Use it for | What IAMS pre-loads |
|---|---|---|
| **IT Audit** | Information-security and IT general controls – access, change, backup, logging, network. Also the home of the **System/IT audit toolkit** ([chapter 15](/help/center?a=ch-sysaudit)). | Controls based on ISO 27001 (e.g. access control rules, backups, security event logging, network controls); *Standard IT Audit Working Paper* (7 sections). |
| **Systems Audit** | Infrastructure and platforms – baselines, change control (CAB), disaster recovery, capacity. | Controls such as `SYS-INF-001` baseline configuration, `SYS-CHG-001` change advisory board, `SYS-DR-001` disaster recovery, `SYS-CAP-001` capacity. |
| **Financial Audit** | Payments, reconciliations, fixed assets, treasury. | Controls such as `FIN-AP-001` maker-checker segregation of payment approvals, `FIN-REC-001` monthly bank reconciliations, `FIN-FA-001` fixed-asset register and verification; *Standard Financial Audit Working Paper*. |
| **Compliance Audit** | Regulatory and standards compliance – GDPR/NDPR, ISO 9001, ISO 22301, internal policy. | A larger set (12 default controls, e.g. `ISO9001-9.2` internal audits, `ISO22301-8.2` business impact analysis, GDPR articles); *Standard Compliance Audit Working Paper* (regulatory requirement → criteria → test → evidence → status → conclusion). |
| **Operational Audit** | Efficiency of operations, standard operating procedures, OLA/KPI performance. | Operational controls; *Standard Operational Audit Working Paper*. |
| **Pension Audit** | Pension remittance and retirement benefits (PENCOM / PRA 2014) – PFA reconciliation. | Pension controls (e.g. monthly remittance checks); *Standard Pension Audit Working Paper*. |
| **Procurement Audit** | Tendering, bid evaluation, vendor selection and contract award. | Procurement controls (e.g. bid-opening and bid-evaluation controls). |
| **HR & Payroll Audit** | Payroll integrity – nominal-roll reconciliation, joiners/movers/leavers, statutory deductions. | HR & payroll controls; *Standard HR & Payroll Audit Working Paper* (nominal roll, joiners/movers/leavers, statutory deductions). |
| **Project / Capital Audit** | Capital projects and delivery. | Project controls. |
| **Special Investigation / Audit** | One-off reviews triggered by an incident or request. | A short special-review control set. |

> **Tip:** The pre-loaded controls are only a starting point. In Step 3 of the Start-audit wizard you can edit, remove, add or import controls ([section 7.2](/help/center?a=wizard)). Administrators maintain the defaults under **Settings → Checklist Templates** ([section 24.4](/help/center?a=set-checklists)).

### How the audit-type differences show up in practice

| Stage | What is different by type |
|---|---|
| **Programme** | One programme = one audit type; the approval chain can differ per type ([section 24.5](/help/center?a=cust)). |
| **Wizard step 3** | Different pre-loaded controls. |
| **Working papers** | Different default template (the template drop-down lists all; one is marked **Default** per type). |
| **Findings** | The finding **Category** defaults to the engagement's audit type. |
| **Escalation** | Each type has its own wait times for L1–L4 escalation ([section 16.3](/help/center?a=escalations)). |

articles.title: Audit Modules – dedicated workspaces
articles.text: The Audit Modules menu group gives a focused view of engagements for three domains: System/IT Audit , Financial Audit and Compliance Audit . They are the same engagements as Audit Lifecycle → Engagements, filtered to one domain, with a header that states the control frameworks that apply. articles.title: System Audit toolkit

articles.title: Toolkit overview
articles.body:
Choose **System Audit → Toolkit overview**.

![System audit toolkit – the seven activities and where IAMS covers each](/help/sysaudit-overview.jpg)

The counters show **Analyses run**, **Access reviews**, **Security tests** and **Documents** (with how many are past their review date). Below them, seven numbered tiles map the standard system-audit activities to IAMS tools:

| # | Activity | IAMS tools |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Risk assessment & planning** | Risk register, risk-ranked audit programme, configuration baseline review |
| 2 | **Internal control evaluation** | Event monitoring, change-management review, IT control library, policies & procedures library |
| 3 | **Compliance audits** | Framework coverage (ISO, NDPR, GDPR, SOX ITGC, COBIT), IT contracts & OLAs (expiry tracking), audit trail |
| 4 | **Security audits** | User access reviews & segregation of duties, security testing (VAPT) coordination, continuity & incident-response plans |
| 5 | **Data & system integrity review** | Data analytics (integrity checks, change, backup, incident, logs) |
| 6 | **Audit reporting & follow-up** | Raise findings from exceptions; engagement review |
| 7 | **Monitoring & continuous assurance** | Continuous monitoring, event monitoring |

Each tile lists the *privilege* an auditor needs (for example “Read-only access to configuration settings”) and has shortcut chips that open the tool.

articles.title: Data analytics
articles.body:
Choose **System Audit → Data analytics** for every analysis ever run.

![Data analytics register](/help/sysaudit-analytics.jpg)

Each row: **Reference** (SAR-2026-0020), **Analysis** type and system, **Source** (*Uploaded export* or *IAMS (live)*), **Records** analysed, **Exceptions** by severity, **Review** status (*N open*, *Ready to sign off*, *Signed off*) and **Run** date. Filter by analysis type, source and review status, or search by title, system or reference.

### The analyses available

| Analysis | What it tests |
|---|---|
| **User access review** | Segregation-of-duties conflicts, leavers who still have access, dormant and privileged accounts, sign-in without MFA. |
| **Change management review** | Unapproved, late-approved and self-approved changes; changes with no test evidence. |
| **Backup & recovery verification** | Success rate, failed jobs, systems at risk, overdue or failed restore tests. |
| **Incident management review** | SLA compliance, resolution-SLA breaches, aged open incidents. |
| **Security log anomaly analysis** | Brute-force and password-spray bursts, off-hours privileged actions, cleared audit logs. |
| **Configuration baseline review** | Drifted, missing and insecure settings against a baseline. |
| **Vulnerability scan results** | Critical/high findings and overdue remediation. |
| **Data integrity checks** | Duplicate keys, missing mandatory fields, control-total and record-count agreement, date-range checks. |

### Run a new analysis

*Who can do this: audit manager, audit lead, auditor, super admin.*

**Step 1.** Click **New analysis**.

![New analysis form](/help/sysaudit-new-analysis.jpg)

**Step 2.** Choose the **Analysis**. A hint box explains what it tests and lists the **control references** the results provide evidence for (for example ISO27001-A.5.18, SOX-ITGC-AC).

**Step 3.** Choose the **Data source**: **Uploaded export**, **IAMS (live)** or **Entra ID (live)** (the last two only for the analyses that support them).

**Step 4.** For an upload, type the **System** the data came from (e.g. “Dynafin”, “FW-CORE-01”), optionally a **Title**, and choose an **Engagement** to link the run (otherwise it is organisation-wide). Optionally link a planned **Security test**.

**Step 5.** Under **Export file** click **Choose File** (CSV, TSV or Excel – the first row must be column headers). IAMS previews the columns and asks you to map them (for example which column holds the user name or status).

**Step 6.** Open **Rules & thresholds** to adjust the optional rules (defaults follow good practice).

**Step 7.** Click **Run analysis**. You are taken to the result page.

![The form filled in for a user-access review of an uploaded HR listing](/help/analysis-new-filled.jpg)

After you choose the file, IAMS shows its name, the number of rows and columns, and a **Column mapping** box. It pre-selects columns whose headers it recognises (here *user*, *role*, *status*, *last_login*); change any drop-down, or leave a field as “— not in file —”. **Date format in the file** tells IAMS whether 03/04/2026 means 3 April or 4 March.

![Column mapping and date format](/help/analysis-column-mapping.jpg)

### Read the result and handle exceptions

For a **User access review** the result page has an **Accounts** tab (a *review worksheet*) as well as **Exceptions**:

![Result of a user-access review – summary tiles, rules triggered, provenance and the accounts worksheet](/help/analysis-result.jpg)

**Decide on each account.** Tick one or more accounts and choose:

| Decision | What IAMS asks for | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Appropriate** | A justification for privileged accounts or accounts with a segregation-of-duties conflict (not for ordinary accounts). | Records that the access is justified. |
| **Revoke** | A written recommendation of what should be removed. | **IAMS records the recommendation – the system owner makes the change in the source system.** |
| **Modify** | A recommendation of what should change. | Same – recorded only. |

![Recommending that access be revoked](/help/analysis-revoke-dialog.jpg)

![The decision is shown on the account row](/help/analysis-after-revoke.jpg)

**Handle the exceptions.** On the **Exceptions** tab tick rows and choose **Confirm**, **False positive**, **Explained** or **Reopen**. **Explained** and **False positive** ask for a note, which is kept in the audit trail.

![Exceptions with their severity and disposition](/help/analysis-exceptions-tab.jpg)

![A confirmed exception](/help/analysis-exception-confirmed.jpg)

**Raise a finding.** Tick confirmed exceptions and click **Raise finding**. Choose the **Engagement** it belongs to (the analysis itself is organisation-wide), edit the **Title**, **Severity**, **Category** and **Due date**, optionally describe the **Condition**, and complete **Root cause**, **Risk implication**, **Recommendation** and the **Auditee**. The exception then shows “Finding: …” and stays **Confirmed**.

![Raise audit finding from an exception](/help/analysis-raise-finding-form.jpg)

![The exception is now linked to a finding](/help/analysis-finding-raised.jpg)

> **Note:** An exception that already has a finding cannot be included in a bulk *Explained* or *False positive* action – untick it first.

**Sign off.** **Sign off review** is available only when **every account has a decision and no exceptions are left open**. Click it, add a note and confirm. The page then shows “Signed off”, who signed and when, and the sign-off note; the results are locked as evidence.

![The sign-off dialog](/help/analysis-signoff-dialog.jpg)

![Signed off](/help/analysis-signed-off.jpg)

![An analysis result: provenance, exceptions and dispositions](/help/sysaudit-analysis-detail.jpg)

- **Summary tiles** – the key measures (e.g. success rate 57.1%, failed jobs 3).
- **Rules triggered** – each rule that produced exceptions, with counts.
- **Provenance** – system, records analysed, file name, **SHA-256** fingerprint, who ran it and when, and the control references it evidences. Use **Original extract** to download the exact file.
- **Exceptions** tab – every exception with its **severity** and **disposition**. Filter by rule, severity or disposition; export to **Excel** or **CSV**.

**To disposition exceptions:** tick one or more rows, then choose **Confirm** (a real issue), **False positive**, **Explained** (legitimate reason – add the explanation), or **Reopen**. **Raise finding** turns confirmed exceptions into a finding on an engagement.

When no exceptions remain open, **Sign off review** becomes available. Signing off records who accepted the analysis.

articles.title: Access reviews
articles.body:
Choose **System Audit → Access reviews** to verify who has access to each system, and that nobody holds conflicting duties – without changing anything in the system.

![Access reviews – three ways to run a review](/help/sysaudit-access-reviews.jpg)

 (e.g. “22 SoD”, “14 no MFA”), exceptions by severity and review status. Open one to handle exceptions exactly as in [section 15.2](/help/center?a=sys-analytics).

articles.title: Event monitoring
articles.body:
Choose **System Audit → Event monitoring** for a read-only view of activity in IAMS itself.

articles.title: Continuous monitoring
articles.body:
Choose **System Audit → Continuous monitoring**. IAMS re-runs read-only checks **daily at 06:30**; serious new exceptions notify system-audit administrators.

![Continuous monitoring](/help/sysaudit-monitoring.jpg)

- Counters: **Open exceptions** (latest checks), **Failed sign-ins**, **System exceptions**, **Emerging risks**.
- **Automated checks** – IAMS user access & segregation of duties; IAMS sign-in & access anomalies; Entra ID accounts & group access; IMOC incident SLA. Checks whose integration is switched off show the setting needed (for example “Entra ID directory sync is not enabled”).
- **Run checks now** runs them immediately.
- Trend chart of new exceptions in the last 30 days, **Emerging IT risks** from the Risk Register, and the **latest control posture** per analysis kind.

articles.title: Security testing (VAPT)
articles.body:
Choose **System Audit → Security testing** to coordinate vulnerability assessments and penetration tests – scope, written authorisation, report and remediation.

![Security testing register](/help/sysaudit-security-tests.jpg)

A test moves through: **Planned → Authorised → Testing → Awaiting report → Remediation → Closed**.

### Plan a test

**Step 1.** Click **Plan test**.

![Plan security test form](/help/sysaudit-plan-test.jpg)

**Step 2.** Enter the **Title**, **Test type** (e.g. Penetration test), **Performed by** (e.g. External provider), **Provider / team**, optional **Coordinator** (defaults to you), **Planned start** and **Planned end**.

**Step 3.** Write the **Scope** (systems, IP ranges, applications in scope – *and anything explicitly out of scope*) and, optionally, the **Rules of engagement** (testing windows, prohibited techniques, contacts, stop conditions). Optionally link an **Engagement**.

**Step 4.** Click **Plan test**.

![Plan security test form completed](/help/sectest-plan-filled.jpg)

The test is created with a reference (e.g. **SEC-2026-0004**) in the **Planned** stage. The planner sees a note: *“You planned this test, so someone else must authorise it.”* – the **Authorise test** button is disabled for them.

![A planned test – Authorise test is disabled for the coordinator](/help/sectest-planned.jpg)

### Authorise a test

A different authorised person (CAE, director, audit manager or super admin) opens the test, clicks **Authorise test**, writes a confirmation note and clicks **Authorise**. The confirmation reads “You confirm [provider] may test the agreed scope between [dates] under the rules of engagement.”

![Authorise test enabled for the CAE](/help/sectest-authorise-ready.jpg)

![The authorisation note](/help/sectest-authorise-dialog.jpg)

The stage becomes **Authorised** and the **Details** show who authorised it and when.

![Authorised](/help/sectest-authorised.jpg)

> **Important:** A test must be **authorised** before it starts. Authorisation is given by a user holding the authorise permission (CAE, director, audit manager or super admin) and is recorded with the date and name.

### Manage a test

![A test in the Remediation stage](/help/sysaudit-test-detail.jpg)

The page shows the stage tracker, counters (**Scan imports**, **Latest results**, **Open exceptions**, **Findings raised**), **Scope & rules of engagement**, **Details** (provider, planned and actual dates, coordinator, who authorised and when, linked engagement), **Results** (use **Import results** to analyse scanner output; results link to the analysis), **Assets in scope**, and the **Test report** (download or **Upload new version**). **Edit** changes details; **Close test** finishes it.

articles.title: System documentation

Choose **System Audit → System documentation** – the library of policies, procedures, architecture and network diagrams, process manuals, continuity plans and IT contracts that auditors rely on.

articles.title: Requests – ad-hoc sign-offs between colleagues
articles.body:
**Requests** are for approvals and reviews that are *not* audit records – for example “Approve the Q2 budget memo”. Audit records use **Review/Approval** instead.

Choose **Workflow → Requests**.

![Requests page – “To action” and “Requests”](/help/requests-page.jpg)

- **To action** – requests addressed to you that are waiting for your turn.
- **Requests** – requests you raised, so you can follow their progress.
- Filter chips: **All**, **Pending**, **Completed**, **Rejected**, with counts, and a **Filter requests…** box.

### Raise a request

**Step 1.** Click **New request**.

![New request form](/help/requests-new-form.jpg)

**Step 2.** Enter a **Title** (e.g. “Approve Q2 budget memo”) and an optional **Description** giving context.

**Step 3.** Under **Recipients (in order)**, search for people and click to add them. They act **one after another, in the order you add them**.

**Step 4.** Optionally attach files (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, PDF, CSV or images – up to 50 MB each).

**Step 5.** Click **Create request**. Each recipient is notified when it is their turn.

![Recipient added in order](/help/request-recipients-added.jpg)

The panel confirms “Your request has been sent” with its reference (for example **REQ-2026-0002**); **Open request** takes you to it.

![Request sent](/help/request-sent.jpg)

**The request page** shows the **Details**, **Attachments** (with **Upload file**), the **Recipients** (who is *Current*) and the **Activity** trail with an **Add a comment** box and **Verify signatures**. The sender can **Cancel request**.

![The request as the sender sees it](/help/request-detail.jpg)

**What the recipient sees.** The recipient finds it under **Requests → To action** and, on their turn, gets **Approve**, **Upload Document**, **View & Sign Document** and **Reject**.

![The recipient's request list](/help/request-cae-inbox.jpg)

![The recipient's action panel](/help/request-cae-actions.jpg)

After the last recipient approves, the request is **Completed**, the activity trail shows each comment and approval, and a **Signed documents → Signature certificate** is available with **View** and **Download**.

![A completed request with its signature certificate](/help/request-completed.jpg)

Recipients open the request and choose **Approve** or **Reject**, can **add a comment**, attach files and sign. You can **cancel** a request you raised while it is pending.

articles.title: Users

Choose **System → Users**.

- Each row shows the person's initials, name and e-mail, **Job title**, **Department**, **Roles** and **Status**.

### Create a user

**Step 1.** Click **New User**.

![New user form](/help/user-new-form.jpg)

**Step 2.** Enter **First Name**, **Last Name** and **Email** (all required). Add **Job Title** and **Department** if known.

**Step 3.** Add **Skills** – type a skill (for example ISO 27001, ITGC, SOX) and press **Enter** or comma. Skills are used to rank people when assigning audits.

**Step 4.** Set **Max concurrent engagements** if this person should have a workload cap different from the system default (leave blank to use the default).

**Step 5.** Choose one or more **Roles** from the drop-down, then click **Create user**.

![Choosing roles – each role is listed with its description](/help/user-role-list.jpg)

> **Tip:** If you press **Esc** with unsaved entries, IAMS asks “Discard unsaved changes?” – choose **Keep editing** to carry on.

![The discard-changes guard](/help/user-discard-guard.jpg)

![A completed form](/help/user-form-filled.jpg)

After **Create user** the list shows “User created and onboarding email sent” and the new person at the top of the list.

![User created](/help/user-created.jpg)

> **Tip:** Staff who sign in with their GBB domain account are created automatically the first time they log in, with the default role set by the administrator. Use this form for people who need a specific role from day one, or for local-password accounts.

### View a user

Click **View** to open the **User Profile** panel: contact details, department, job title, **Max concurrent engagements**, **Last login**, **Roles** and a full list of effective **Permissions**.

![User Profile panel](/help/user-view-panel.jpg)

### Edit, deactivate and delete

- **Edit** – change names, job title, department, skills, workload cap and roles.

  *The e-mail address is shown greyed out – it cannot be changed.*

![Edit user](/help/user-edit-form.jpg)
- **Deactivate** – immediately blocks sign-in without removing history. **Activate** restores it. Prefer this over deleting.

  IAMS asks for confirmation (“This blocks the user from signing in until reactivated.”). The row then shows **Inactive** and the button becomes **Activate**.

![Deactivate confirmation](/help/user-deactivate-confirm.jpg)

![An inactive user](/help/user-deactivated.jpg)
- **Delete** – removes the account from the active list (the audit trail keeps its history).

> **Important:** Removing a role removes the corresponding menu items and permissions at that person's next page load. If you remove the *only* role from a user they see a “No roles assigned” screen until a role is added.

articles.title: Audit Customization
articles.body:
The most powerful tab: it controls how the audit lifecycle behaves.

![Audit Customization – lifecycle gates, OLA rules, approval matrix and taxonomy](/help/settings-customization.jpg)

| Section | What you control |
|---|---|
| **Lifecycle Gates** | Four switches: *Require all checklists tested* (before Quality Review), *Require approved working paper*, *Require issued review* (before Review Issued), *Require closed findings* (before Closed). Turning a switch off removes that requirement. |
| **OLA Rules** | Default **engagement turnaround** (30 days), **finding due window** (90), **high-risk finding** window (60) and **critical finding** window (30) – used to pre-fill due dates. |
| **Approval Matrix** | The ordered chain of approvers per record type (e.g. *Audit Review*): each **stage** names the permission required and optionally a *designated approver*, or “any qualified staff holding this permission”. Add, reorder or remove stages. The first stage can automatically resolve to the engagement's own manager. |
| **Audit Taxonomy** | The lists that populate drop-downs: audit types, priorities, finding categories and finding severities. Add or remove values with the chips. |
| **Planning Priority Weights** | How the composite priority in the programme's *Add plan* screen is calculated (risk score, unresolved findings, time since last audit). |
| **Analytics Visibility** | Which analytics sections are shown. |

Click **Save changes** under each section after editing.

Scrolling down shows the **Approval Matrix** in full: separate chains for **Audit Review** (stages such as *Engagement Manager*, *Report Approve Oversight* and *Report Approve Final*), **Audit Programme** (*Plan Approve*), **Working Paper** (*Engagement Manager*) and **Finding Closure** (*Engagement Manager*). Each stage has a drop-down for the permission required and a *Select Staff Member (Designated Approver)* box – leave it as “Any qualified staff holding this permission” or pin a named person. **Add approval level** appends a stage; the arrows re-order stages and the bin removes one. The **Audit Taxonomy** lists (audit types, priorities, finding severities and categories) are edited with chips.

![Approval Matrix](/help/settings-matrix.jpg)

Further down, **Analytics Visibility** switches analytics sections on and off, and **Planning Priority Weights** sets how the recommended-audit priority is calculated – by default **Risk Score 40**, **Open Findings 25**, **Overdue For Audit 20**, **Never Audited 10** (weights are normalised by their sum).

![Analytics visibility and planning weights](/help/settings-weights.jpg)

> **Important:** Relaxing a lifecycle gate lets engagements move on without that evidence. Do so only with the CAE's agreement – it is recorded in the audit trail.

articles.title: Directory
articles.body:
![Directory – map Azure AD groups to IAMS roles](/help/settings-directory.jpg)

When Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) is connected, you can grant roles automatically by group membership.

1. Click **New mapping**.
2. Choose the **Azure AD group** and the **IAMS role** that members should receive.
3. Save. Members receive the role the next time they sign in or when you click **Sync now**.

![New group mapping form](/help/directory-mapping-form.jpg)

The form asks for the **Azure group Object ID** (the GUID from Entra ID, not the display name), a **Group display name** (for readability) and the **IAMS role** to grant.

Roles granted this way are marked as directory-driven so they are not confused with roles assigned by hand.

articles.body:

articles.title: Troubleshooting
articles.body:
| What you see | Why it happens | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **Sign-in takes 15 seconds, then “Invalid credentials”** | IAMS first tries your directory account (Active Directory), waits for it to reply, then checks the password stored in IAMS. | Wait for the reply; then check your username/e-mail and password. If it persists, ask an administrator to confirm your account exists and is active. |
| **“Too many requests. Please try again in … seconds”** | A protective rate limit on the server (heavy use, or many tabs open). | Wait the number of seconds shown and try again. Close unused IAMS tabs. |
| **“You submitted this item for approval and cannot also approve it”** | Segregation of duties ([section 6.5](/help/center?a=sod)). | Ask a different authorised person to approve. |
| **A menu item, tab or button is missing** | Your role does not include it, or the tab is padlocked. | Check **Profile → Access**; ask your administrator if you need the permission. |
| **“No findings yet” in an auditee's Follow-up tab** | Findings are hidden from auditees until the review is issued ([section 3.2](/help/center?a=findingflow)). | Wait until the audit team issues the review. |
| **An engagement will not move to Quality Assurance** | A gate is unmet. | Open the engagement and read **What's next**: finish checklist testing and get all working papers approved. |
| **Working paper is read-only** | It is **Submitted** (awaiting approval). | Wait for the manager; if it is **Rejected**, edit and resubmit. |
| **“You submitted this item … cannot also approve it”** on a security test or other item | The person who plans/submits cannot authorise/approve the same item. | Ask a different authorised person (for security tests: CAE, director, audit manager or super admin other than the coordinator). |
| **“Exceptions already raised as findings stay confirmed”** | You included an exception that already has a finding in a bulk action. | Untick that row and repeat the action for the others. |
| **“Discard unsaved changes?” when pressing Esc on a form** | The panel has edits that have not been saved. | Choose **Keep editing** to carry on, or **Discard changes** to lose them. |
| **Sign off review is greyed out on an analysis** | Some account decisions or exceptions are still pending. | Give every account a decision (Appropriate / Revoke / Modify) and disposition every exception first. |
| **“Failed to load data. Try again”** | A temporary connection problem. | Click **Try again**; if it keeps failing, check your network and tell the administrator. |
| **E-mail notifications not arriving** | E-mail (SMTP) may not be configured on the server. | In-app notifications still work. Ask the administrator to configure e-mail. |

articles.title: Frequently asked questions
articles.body:
**Can I edit a finding after raising it?** Yes, while the engagement is open; the audit trail records each change.

**Who sees my draft working paper?** Members of the audit team who have working-paper access to that engagement. Auditees cannot open the Working Papers tab.

**Why can't I approve my own submission?** To keep approvals independent. Another authorised user must approve.

**How do I know what an engagement is waiting for?** Read **What's next** under the stage tracker.

**Where do I find a signed approval document?** On the approved item (for a programme: its page; for any approval: **Review/Approval → History → Signed document**).

**How do I get a report for management?** Use **Periodic Reports** ([section 10.4](/help/center?a=periodic)) or **Analytics → Committee pack (PDF)**.

articles.title: Appendix A – Glossary
articles.body:
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Auditee** | The person or department being audited; responds to findings. |
| **Audit Universe** | Register of everything that can be audited, with risk scores. |
| **Audit Programme** | The approved annual plan of audits for one audit type. |
| **Plan / plan item** | One entity to be audited, scheduled within a programme. |
| **Engagement** | A single audit, from planning to closure. |
| **Checklist / control test** | A control to be tested, with a result: Passed, Failed, Not applicable. |
| **Working paper** | The documented record of audit work, approved by a manager. |
| **Evidence** | Files supporting audit conclusions. |
| **Finding** | An issue raised in an audit, with severity, root cause, risk and recommendation. |
| **Review / report** | The formal audit report, approved and issued. |
| **Follow-up** | The process of remediation, verification and closure of findings. |
| **OLA** | Operational-level agreement – the target completion date of an engagement. |
| **Escalation** | Automatic notification of the next level when something is overdue. |
| **SoD** | Segregation of duties – no one approves their own submission. |
| **CAE** | Chief Audit Executive. |
| **SHA-256** | A digital fingerprint of an uploaded file proving it has not been altered. |
| **VAPT** | Vulnerability assessment and penetration testing. |
| **Attestation** | An owner's confirmation that an asset record is accurate. |
